pillar_reactions.evidence: Agreed with the substance — 'Yeah. Yeah. Sounds good' and 'I think so. Yeah' to whether the approach would work — but returned twice with mechanics questions rather than value questions. On form: 'I really want to, yeah, I'm just really concerned about form, getting the right form', reinforced by 'I see on social media, like people posting their videos and then I look at the comments... it's overwhelming.' On scheduling: 'When it comes to, like, workout schedule, you say three or four times a week. So, how do you break it out for the week? Is it three consecutive days, four consecutive days?' He also engaged specifically with the core claim, volunteering 'my core, I have to focus on my core. My core is really weak' when the rep raised it.

Clean acceptance — 'No, looks fine' — and he immediately volunteered a bridge the rep could use: 'actually my wife does the intermittent fasting.' He then explained his own history with it honestly, that he had avoided it because 'in the morning I started making mistakes at work', but that he already trains fasted with only bone broth beforehand. The pillar required almost no work because the rep had already validated 90% of his diet during baseline; the only substantive addition was protein intake, which the rep flagged and deferred to Trevor.

Agreed throughout and named exactly why it mattered to him: 'That's, that's good. Just to be able to modify it, because I wouldn't, yeah, like this journey has always, it's just really been on my own and just be just trying to, I feel like, I just need some guidance.' The programme-flexes-around-your-life framing landed against a genuine constraint — dual US and Asia market hours plus a three-week holiday. The rep followed with the elite-athletes-have-coaches argument and got the strongest concession of the call: 'Yeah, I'm not smart enough, man. I came to that conclusion. I need guidance. Let me try it. Let me try the coaching.'

anchors.raw: It's not the cheapest, it's the one that you're going to be working with Trevor, one-on-one. Yeah? Because we can get you on working with one of Trevor's coaches, but I think with your condition, with this lower back, Sayadeka, that's something I think Trevor would need to, to have his look on.
anchors.note: The most significant anchor in this batch because it is internal and previously unrecorded anywhere in the corpus. A cheaper coaching tier with a non-Trevor coach exists, the buyer asked for its price twice — 'Is that the cheapest?' and 'I need a little bit lower amount if it's not working with Trevor' — and no figure was ever given. The steer up was justified on clinical grounds, which means the prospect's spinal condition was used as a reason to pay more rather than as a reason to seek clearance.

anchors.raw: Or you can even use the third-party financing option, like Pava. We use Pava, and you can spread it even over 12 months. And that's going to be, like, $650 per month.
anchors.note: Rep-introduced and rep-preferred: financing was the first structure offered, at roughly $7,800 total against a $6,000 price. The prospect, who works in investment management, read the schedule and reversed it himself — 'I noticed that with these options, it's more than 6,000 at the end' — then asked for a full-payment link and paid on a credit card. The deal improved by $1,800 in fees avoided because the buyer was financially literate, not because the rep steered him there.

anchors.raw: when I was looking at the videos, I was just a little concerned about my age, or it seemed like it was targeting like the 30, 40-year-olds.
anchors.note: The opening line of the call was a fit doubt, not a price doubt. Marketing is reading as 30-40 targeted while the rep says 'majority is around 40-ish plus. And recently, a lot of 60 plus guys are coming in.' A visible mismatch between who the content addresses and who is actually buying, and it nearly cost a $6,000 sale before it started.

anchors.raw: I'm already there for frickin' two hours... But that's like bonding time with me and my wife, and I don't want to lose that, but at the same time, it's like I need to be more efficient.
anchors.competitor: Gym membership plus turbo kick and cardio classes
anchors.note: The competing spend is time rather than money — two hours in the gym, plus cardio classes with his wife, plus an aspiration to add yoga. Time efficiency was the strongest value lever available and the rep used it well. Note the unresolved tension: the classes are marital time he does not want to give up, and nobody established how the new programme sits alongside them.

unmet_demand.want: To break a four-to-five-month sciatica flare cycle that has cost him a month of function at a time and ruined two holidays
unmet_demand.why_unmet: No clinical layer exists in the offer, and his only current clinical contact is a chiropractor. The rep asserted a mechanism — that stretching without strengthening means 'it's gonna show up every single time', and that his heel pain is because 'your body is... weak' — but that is a coaching claim about a diagnosed spinal condition with radicular symptoms in two regions. Whether loaded ballistic training reduces or provokes this cycle is genuinely unknown and nobody suggested a physician establish it. He is buying a clinical outcome and the sale is priced on it.

unmet_demand.want: A cheaper coaching option, asked for explicitly and twice
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The tier exists — the rep said so — and was never priced. The buyer was steered to the premium option on clinical grounds and complied. This is not a product gap; the product exists and was withheld.

unmet_demand.want: To keep doing cardio classes with his wife, which he described as bonding time he does not want to lose, while cutting total training hours
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Never addressed. The rep's pitch was three to four sessions of 30-40 minutes replacing a six-day split, but said nothing about how the classes fit alongside it or whether they count toward recovery load. Given that the classes are the emotional reason he trains at all and that his stated deep why is his relationship with his wife, leaving this unanswered is a real retention risk.

unmet_demand.want: Yoga-level flexibility, which he has tried and cannot access because he is not flexible enough to do the class
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Partially claimed through the mobility protocols but never scoped. He said 'I tried yoga, but I just don't have that flexibility and mobility yet', and the rep did not return to it. Plausible that the mobility work serves it; nothing on the call establishes that it does.
